header: Colour: RGB <-> HEX <-> HSL, the arithmetic and the reading of a typed line (pure, no React). A colour is three whole numbers from 0 to 255 (red, green, blue); its HEX form is "#" and two hexadecimal digits for each, "#4F46E5". A short HEX of three digits ("#f53") means each digit doubled ("#ff5533"). HSL is the same colour as a hue (the angle on the colour wheel, 0 to 360 degrees), a saturation and a lightness (each 0 to 100 per cent), "hsl(243, 75%, 59%)". I show HSL in whole numbers (as a stylesheet writes it), so a colour typed in HSL comes back as the nearest RGB, which can differ by a point from the RGB it was first read from. Nothing is stored or sent; the card is in ColourPanel.tsx.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_HEX
doc: The colour I open a bare "rgb to hex" question with (the intranet's own indigo)

symbols.name: toHex
symbols.sig: export function toHex({ r, g, b }: Rgb): string
doc: I write it as "#4F46E5": upper case, always six digits

symbols.name: cssRgb
symbols.sig: export function cssRgb({ r, g, b }: Rgb): string
doc: Gives "rgb(79, 70, 229)", as a stylesheet writes it

symbols.name: parseChannel
symbols.sig: export function parseChannel(text: string): number | null
doc: A channel typed in a box: a whole number from 0 to 255 and nothing else ("12", " 255 "); anything else is not a channel (I do no rounding and no clamping: a wrong number is shown as wrong)

symbols.name: parseChannels
symbols.sig: export function parseChannels(r: string, g: string, b: string): Rgb | null
doc: Reads the three boxes as a colour; returns null while any of them is not a channel

symbols.name: parseHex
symbols.sig: export function parseHex(text: string): Rgb | null
doc: I accept a HEX typed in a box with or without "#", three or six digits ("#4f46e5", "4F46E5", "#f53"); null otherwise

symbols.name: rgbToHsl
symbols.sig: export function rgbToHsl({ r, g, b }: Rgb): Hsl
doc: Gives the hue, saturation and lightness of a colour, in whole numbers: hue 0 to 359 degrees, saturation and lightness 0 to 100 per cent ("#FF5733" is hsl(11, 100%, 60%))

symbols.name: hslToRgb
symbols.sig: export function hslToRgb({ h, s, l }: Hsl): Rgb
doc: Returns the RGB of a hue (degrees, 360 is 0), a saturation and a lightness (per cent); I round each channel to a whole number

symbols.name: cssHsl
symbols.sig: export function cssHsl({ h, s, l }: Hsl): string
doc: Gives "hsl(11, 100%, 60%)", as a stylesheet writes it

symbols.name: parseHslPart
symbols.sig: export function parseHslPart(text: string, max: number): number | null
doc: I accept a hue, saturation or lightness typed in a box as a number from 0 up to `max` (the hue to 360, the others to 100), with or without a % or a degree sign; decimals are allowed; anything else is not one

symbols.name: parseHslBoxes
symbols.sig: export function parseHslBoxes(h: string, s: string, l: string): Hsl | null
doc: Reads the three boxes as an HSL colour; returns null while any of them is not valid

symbols.name: stepPart
symbols.sig: export function stepPart(text: string, dir: number, min: number, max: number, fallback: number): string
doc: Moves the box's text up or down by `dir` (1 or -1, or 10 with Shift), kept between `min` and `max`; I step text that is not a number from `fallback` (the colour's own value for that box)

symbols.name: inkOn
symbols.sig: export function inkOn({ r, g, b }: Rgb): "#0f172a" | "#ffffff"
doc: I pick black or white, whichever reads better on this colour (judged by the perceived brightness, 0 to 255)

symbols.name: parseColour
symbols.sig: export function parseColour(raw: string): ColourAsk | null
doc: The typed line: "#ff5733 to rgb", "hex ff5733", "#f53", "#ff5733 to hsl", "rgb(255, 87, 51) to hex", "rgb 255 87 51", "255,87,51 to hex", "hsl(11, 100%, 60%)", "hsl 11 100 60 to rgb", and the bare question "rgb to hex" / "hex to rgb" / "hex to hsl" / "rgb to hex to hsl" / "colour converter" (which opens with DEFAULT_HEX). I take a line for a colour only when it says so: a "#", the word "hex", "rgb" or "hsl", or "to hex"; that way an ordinary number or a word like "bad" or "add" (three hex digits) is never read as a colour. Returns the colour as a six-digit HEX, or null.

behaviours: 0,0,0 is #000000 and 255,255,255 is #FFFFFF (two digits each, zero-padded)
a small number is padded: 1,2,3 is #010203; 10,11,12 is #0A0B0C (upper case)
the intranet's indigo, 79,70,229, is #4F46E5
the stylesheet form is rgb(79, 70, 229)
#FF5733 is 255,87,51; with or without #, any case
a short HEX doubles each digit: #f53 is #ff5533 is 255,85,51; #000 and #fff
not a HEX: 4 or 5 digits, 7 digits, a letter past F, empty, two #
every colour survives the round trip, HEX -> RGB -> HEX and RGB -> HEX -> RGB (all 256 values of each channel)
a channel is a whole number 0 to 255: 0, 7, 255, ' 12 '
not a channel: 256, -1, 1.5, 12a, empty, 1e2, 1000 (never rounded or clamped)
three boxes make a colour only when all three are channels
the pure colours: red 0, yellow 60, green 120, cyan 180, blue 240, magenta 300 degrees, all at 100% and 50%
greys have no saturation and no hue: black hsl(0, 0%, 0%), white hsl(0, 0%, 100%), 128 grey hsl(0, 0%, 50%)
the hue never reaches 360: a colour just short of red round the wheel (255,0,1) is hue 0, not 360
the pure colours come back exactly: hsl(0,100%,50%) is #FF0000, 120 is #00FF00, 240 is #0000FF, 60 is #FFFF00, 180 is #00FFFF, 300 is #FF00FF
black and white and a grey, whatever the hue: lightness 0 is #000000, 100 is #FFFFFF, saturation 0 at 50% is #808080
hue 360 is hue 0 (red) and a negative or large hue wraps round the wheel
HSL is shown in whole numbers, so RGB -> HSL -> RGB is within 3 of each channel (hsl(11, 100%, 60%) is #FF5833, a point from #FF5733), never wrong by more
the stylesheet form is hsl(243, 75%, 59%)
hue 0 to 360, saturation and lightness 0 to 100, with or without % or the degree sign, decimals allowed: '11', '360', '11°', '100%', '50.5', ' 7 '
not an HSL part: hue 361, saturation 101, -1, 'abc', '', '1e2', '5%%'
three boxes make an HSL colour only when all three are valid
black ink on white and yellow, white ink on black and indigo
a HEX with # is a colour: '#ff5733', '#FF5733 to rgb', '#f53', '#ff5733 in rgb', 'css color #fff'
a HEX without # needs the word hex: 'hex ff5733', 'hex code ff5733', 'ff5733 hex to rgb', 'hex #ff5733'

the bare question opens with the default colour: 'rgb to hex', 'hex to rgb', 'rgb to hex converter', 'hex to rgb?', 'colour converter', 'color picker', 'hex code converter', 'hex to hsl', 'hsl to rgb', 'rgb to hex to hsl', 'rgb hex hsl converter'

an HSL is a colour: 'hsl(0, 100%, 50%)', 'hsl 120 100 50', 'hsl(240deg 100% 50%) to hex', 'hsl(11, 100%, 60%) to rgb'; and '#ff5733 to hsl', '255,87,51 to hsl', 'rgb(255,87,51) to hsl' name the colour they hold
not a colour: a plain number or word, hex digits without a hint, a channel out of range, too long
the other conversions are not taken: '5 km in miles', '100 usd to inr', '98.6 f to c', '12*45+7', 'calculator'
stepping a channel: 87 up is 88, down is 86; Shift (10) gives 97
a channel stops at its ends: 255 up stays 255, 0 down stays 0, 250 up by 10 is 255
the hue goes to 360 and no further; saturation and lightness stop at 100
text that is not a number steps from the colour's own value: '' up from 51 is 52, 'x' down from 0 is 0
a % or degree sign and spaces are read as in the boxes: '60%' up is 61, ' 11° ' down is 10; a decimal keeps no float dust: 11.1 up is 12.1
a wrong number is pulled back in range: 300 down in 0..255 is 255
